newsitem.title: USA: USDA says starts potato diversion program.
newsitem.headline: USDA says starts potato diversion program.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department said on Friday it would pay potato growers to divert 1996-crop fresh Irish round white and russet potatoes to charities or for use as livestock feed.

USDA said it would set a payment rate for such diversions. Details would be published soon in the Federal Register. To qualify for the payments, potatoes must meet minimum grade standards and must be inspected by federal or state inspectors.

Earlier this week, USDA said it would purchase $25.5 million worth of potatoes in the surplus removal of 41 million lbs of dehydrated, frozen and canned potatoes. An additional purchase for dehydrated granule potatoes will be announced shortly, it said.
